title: Project Hail Mary
author: Andy Weir
ai_summary: A lone astronaut wakes with amnesia aboard a spacecraft and must piece together his memory and his mission to stop an extinction-level event.
why_read: Hard science that never gets in the way of the heart. The first-contact friendship at its centre is the most joyful thing in modern sci-fi.

title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
ai_summary: A practical framework for building good habits and breaking bad ones by focusing on tiny, compounding changes to systems rather than goals.
why_read: Read it if you keep setting goals and missing them. The chapter on habit stacking alone changes how you plan a morning.

title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
ai_summary: A sweeping account of how Homo sapiens went from an unremarkable ape to the dominant species, driven by shared fictions like money, nations and religion.
why_read: It reframes everything you assumed was permanent as a story we agreed to believe. Uncomfortable in the best way.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
ai_summary: On the desert planet Arrakis, a young heir to a fallen house is drawn into a war over the universe's most valuable resource and into a prophecy he never asked for.
why_read: The blueprint for every epic that came after it. Politics, ecology and religion braided into one story.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
ai_summary: Through the eyes of a child in the Depression-era South, a lawyer defends a Black man falsely accused of rape and the town turns on them both.
why_read: Scout's narration keeps it human rather than preachy. A short book that stays with you for decades.

title: The Catcher in the Rye
author: J.D. Salinger
ai_summary: Expelled from prep school, Holden Caulfield wanders New York City for three days, raging at phoniness while quietly falling apart.
why_read: Everyone argues about whether Holden is insufferable or heartbreaking. Read it and pick a side.

title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows
author: J.K. Rowling
ai_summary: The final year: three friends abandon school to hunt the fragments of a dark wizard's soul before he finishes remaking the world in his image.
why_read: The one where the series stops being about school and starts being about loss. Worth rereading as an adult.

title: The Kite Runner
author: Khaled Hosseini
ai_summary: A privileged boy in Kabul betrays his closest friend, then spends the rest of his life and a return to Taliban-era Afghanistan trying to atone.
why_read: A book about guilt that refuses to let its narrator off easily. Read it for the last quarter.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
ai_summary: A Nobel laureate maps the two systems behind human thought: the fast, intuitive one that runs most of your life, and the slow, deliberate one that rarely checks its work.
why_read: You will catch yourself making the exact errors he describes while reading the chapter that describes them.

title: Being Mortal
author: Atul Gawande
ai_summary: A surgeon examines how modern medicine handles ageing and dying, and argues that prolonging life has crowded out the question of what makes it worth living.
why_read: Hard to start, impossible to put down. It gives you the vocabulary for conversations you have been avoiding with your parents.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
ai_summary: Black holes, the Big Bang and the arrow of time, explained for readers with no physics background and almost no equations.
why_read: The famous book everyone owns and nobody finishes. Read the first four chapters properly and it clicks.

title: The Lean Startup
author: Eric Ries
ai_summary: A method for building companies under extreme uncertainty: ship a minimum viable product, measure real behaviour, and pivot before you run out of runway.
why_read: Dated in its examples, still correct in its argument. The build-measure-learn loop is the part that matters.
